summary: First full testing pass of the Helpdesk/ITSM v2 platform (backend + frontend). Backend: 27/27 pytest tests passing covering auth, admin user management, ticket lifecycle + RabbitMQ auto-assignment, locks, chat/attachment upload, resolve+CSAT, reject, tags, escalation/reassignment approve flow, admin config (algorithm switch + SLA policy edit persistence), kanban, timeline, monitor, and role-based 403 guards. Frontend: exercised via Playwright across employee/technician/admin roles - ticket creation with correct priority badge, live auto-assignment, lock acquire/conflict/force-release, chat with file attachment rendering as clickable /uploads link, resolve -> CSAT survey -> submit -> resubmission blocked, real-time WebSocket notification delivery (bell unread count + auto chat refresh) verified across two concurrent browser contexts without page refresh, SLA panel correctly shown to technician/admin and absent for employee, all admin pages (Users, Tags, Config, Kanban, Timeline, Monitor) render correctly with live data, and all tested role-based route guards (employee blocked from /queue,/my-escalations,/admin/*; technician blocked from /tickets,/tickets/new; unauthenticated redirected to /login) work correctly.

minor.issue: Queue is declared+bound at startup (via connect()) but no backend consumer subscribes to it in gateway/main.py lifespan - this appears intentional since external vtech SDK bots are expected to consume it themselves, but worth confirming with main agent that this is by design and not an oversight.

No brute-force lockout after N failed login attempts, and login issues bearer tokens in JSON body rather than httpOnly cookies. This appears to be an intentional design choice for this custom-built JWT app (not the Emergent Google-auth playbook), but flagging since the review checklist mentions these as auth hygiene items.

action_items: Confirm with main agent whether vtech.queue is intentionally left without a backend-side consumer (external SDK bots consume it directly) - no code change needed if so.
No blocking bugs found; app is in a strong, near production-ready state for this first pass.
critical_code_review_comments: gateway/main.py lifespan is clean and well organized; event bus, seed, indexes, and background jobs are wired correctly.
Consistent use of async/await across service layers; MongoDB _id excluded via serialize_doc pattern.
Role guards implemented both server-side (require_roles dependency) and client-side (ProtectedRoute) - verified redundant/defense-in-depth protection works.
SLA panel role-gating (hidden entirely for employee, not just visually) verified correctly - no DOM leak of SLA data to employee role.
Notification targeting logic (build_targets) is comprehensive and covers all event types described in the problem statement.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows passed (no bugs found across ~9 major flows manually verified via Playwright)

test_credentials: admin/Admin@12345, tech.human/Tech@12345, tech.virtual/VTech@12345, employee.demo/Employee@12345 - all confirmed working, sourced from /app/memory/test_credentials.md
seed_data_creation: Backend pytest created several TEST_-prefixed tickets, tags, and users (some auto-cleaned via delete calls in tests; ticket/message test data intentionally left in DB as it mirrors real usage and was also used for the Playwright frontend pass - e.g. 'TEST PW e2e ticket', 'TEST_ticket priority check', 'TEST_escalation ticket', 'TEST_reject ticket'). These can be cleared by main agent if a clean DB state is desired before user demo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: This was the first comprehensive pass. All 16 feature/bug areas listed in the review request were exercised and passed: registration/pending activation, admin user management, ticket creation+priority matrix, RabbitMQ auto-assignment (confirmed within seconds), lock lifecycle+conflict+force-release, chat+attachment upload+rendering, resolve+CSAT+resubmission-block, reject, tags, escalation approve flow (reassignment approve/reject/return not all individually re-tested in this pass beyond backend pytest which covers 'approve'; frontend UI for reject/return on Monitor page not manually clicked - recommend a follow-up pass specifically clicking monitor-reject-{id}/monitor-return-{id} buttons if not already covered), real-time WS notifications (verified robust, initial 'WebSocket closed before established' console messages during my own testing were a false alarm caused by using page.goto() for full-page reloads mid-session, not a real app bug - a persisted SPA session keeps the WS connection alive fine), SLA role-gating, admin Config/Kanban/Timeline/Monitor pages, and all tested role-based route guards. No blocking issues found. Suggest next agent spot-check the reject/return branches of the reassignment review flow via UI, and do a longer-duration SLA breach timing test if a longer test window is available.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A - no unresolved bugs found in this pass. The one apparent WS anomaly encountered during testing was traced to Playwright's page.goto() causing full browser navigation/reload (which necessarily tears down any in-flight WebSocket handshake), not an application defect; a persistent SPA session (no reload) held the WS connection open reliably and delivered real-time notifications and chat updates correctly.
